selected_evidence.requirement: Record sudo commands with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log
selected_evidence.summary: Effective sudo defaults select the dedicated logfile; the test record contains a timestamp, invoking user root, target user nobody, and executed command.

selected_evidence.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log
selected_evidence.summary: The !syslog default is persistent, and unique pre- and post-reboot markers were absent from messages, secure, and the system journal.

Healthy baseline boot ID was 55595e92-e932-451b-ac1d-75d72072b358; reboot was acknowledged; recovered boot ID was 0024cb92-4dba-4938-901f-3b07669d0d01. After reboot, rsyslog was active, sudoers parsed successfully, the prior record remained, and a new isolated sudo record was written.

commands.command:
MARKER=SUDO_LOG_VERIFY_20261001; BEFORE=$(date --iso-8601=seconds); sudo -u nobody /usr/bin/printf '%s
' "$MARKER"; AFTER=$(date --iso-8601=seconds); printf 'window=%s..%s
' "$BEFORE" "$AFTER"; printf '%s
' '--- dedicated sudo log ---'; grep -F "$MARKER" /var/log/sudo-commands.log; printf '%s
' '--- general log search ---'; FOUND=0; for f in /var/log/messages /var/log/secure; do if [ -f "$f" ] && grep -F "$MARKER" "$f"; then FOUND=1; fi; done; if journalctl --since "$BEFORE" --until "$AFTER" --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep -F "$MARKER"; then FOUND=1; fi; if [ "$FOUND" -eq 0 ]; then echo 'marker absent from /var/log/messages, /var/log/secure, and system journal'; else echo 'marker unexpectedly present in a general log'; exit 1; fi
